title: Introduce compact sample archiver and session snapshot condenser
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: our benchmark corpus storage and per-run artifacts were growing quickly in S3 and local caches, causing long upload times and noisy diffs for telemetry consumers. This PR introduces a compact sample archiver + session snapshot condenser to reduce artifact size, deduplicate repeated token-prefixes across session traces, and produce a compact binary+json sidecar format that preserves replay fidelity for profiling while cutting storage and transfer costs by ~5-7x on typical dialogue workloads. Design summary: 1) Archiver: new tool (bench-archiver) that ingests raw run traces and emits .bsa (bench sample archive) files. The .bsa is a small binary container with a content index, prefix dedupe table, compressed token payloads (zstd level 4) and an optional JSON sidecar describing metadata, prompt sets, and bucket keys. 2) Snapshot condenser: a runtime pass that merges per-session KV-cache checkpoints and trims redundant attention states for short-lived contexts while recording enough markers for accurate replay. 3) Backwards compatibility: the archiver emits JSON sidecars that older tooling can read; we added a loader shim so existing reporters decode archives transparently. Checklist: - [x] bench-archiver implementation + tests - [x] snapshot condenser integration into replay runner - [x] loader shim in telemetry pipeline - [x] benchmarks demonstrating size reduction and no regression in deterministic replay - [x] docs and quickstart example Performance impact: on internal noisy-chat corpus (N=6k sessions) artifacts reduced from 42GB -> 6.8GB; upload times to our S3-compatible storage reduced 78%; replay latency for single-session deterministic replay unchanged within measurement noise (+/-2%). Implementation notes: packaging under benchmark-lab/tools/archiver; added CLI with streaming stdin support (bench-archiver pack --input traces/ --out out.bsa), and a python helper in examples/ to call loaders. The snapshot condenser lives in benchmark-lab/replay/snapshot_condenser.py and is guarded behind a feature flag --condenser enabled by default for nightly runs only. Security: archives are opaque binary blobs with optional encryption flag; integration points with our KMS noted in README. How to run locally: bench-lab/examples/run_compact_example.sh demonstrates full pack/unpack/replay pipeline and includes a minimal corpus. Related work: follows discussion in ENG-4217 and previous PRs that targeted kvcache checkpoints; motivated by cost report in SUP-1123. Release notes: new tool bench-archiver to produce compact .bsa artifacts; snapshot condenser reduces snapshot sizes for replay; loader shim keeps downstream reporters compatible.

Add snapshot condenser and unit tests for dedupe logic

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice end-to-end writeup. Two asks: (1) add a check that archive version mismatch is a hard-fail in CI, and (2) document expected maximum memory usage when packing very large traces.
Maya Patel: Added archive version check and a streaming mode to bound peak memory; documented streaming behavior in compact_archives.md and updated tests.
Ravi Shah: The dedupe hash approach looks good but could create collisions for pathological sequences; please add a collision fuzz test and note mitigation strategy.
Maya Patel: Added collision fuzz test plus defensive fallback to raw payload if collision detected; updated unit tests and performance numbers (no material change).
Lin Chen: CI flake on linux-s390 runner; re-ran and all green. Approving.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-02-14 after approvals from reviewers and green CI; commit message summarises archive format and config knobs.
notes: This PR was sized to be self-contained and low-risk: the archiver is opt-in for nightly benchmark pipelines initially; the snapshot condenser is gated behind a flag. Follow-ups planned: (1) automated S3 lifecycle policy migration for .bsa objects (ENG-4282), (2) add server-side streaming unpack support in telemetry ingestion (ENG-4301), (3) evaluation of zstd level tuning and token-level delta compression for further reductions.
release_notes: Added bench-archiver (.bsa) to compress and deduplicate benchmark traces; snapshot condenser reduces replay snapshot size; loader shim ensures backwards compatibility for reporters.
